title: Four Packets of Papad and a Borrowed Rs 80 on a Girgaum Terrace
conflicts: Early growth: BBC and WIPO say 25 members within three months, Popat (2021) said about 25 by the end of year one and 300 within two years, the World Bank case says 300 in three years; story attributes the three-month figure to the BBC and says 'within three years'. First sale: nearby grocery shop (Popat) vs local merchant (WIPO) vs Bhuleshwar merchant (Wikipedia); story says 'a shop nearby'. Two conflicting accounts of how the name Lijjat was chosen, so it is omitted. Popat's age differs across sources and an unconfirmed 2023 death date exists, so no claim is made about her now.
notes: Founder interviews: BBC 2009 (English quotes used) and Gujarati Mid-day 2021 (read in Gujarati, paraphrased only). Stance is 'complicates': Montaigne's preference for living by right not favour against a cooperative that began on a borrowed Rs 80.
